title: Progressive Legibility and Tool Orchestration PRD (draft)
overview: Working PRD sketch for a progressive (incremental) output model + deterministic tool orchestration contract and recommended SDK ergonomics. Goal is to let product engineers receive increasingly legible partial results, make safe tool calls early, and reconcile streamed patches into final structured outputs with minimal client bookkeeping.
goals: 1) Reduce end-to-end perceived latency by surfacing progressively clearer incremental outputs. 2) Provide deterministic semantics for tool calls from partial outputs (avoid double-invocation, enable idempotency). 3) Offer SDK patterns that keep client code simple for both evented (WebSocket/SSE) and synchronous (HTTP) consumers. 4) Ensure observability hooks and telemetry for cost/latency attribution per-frame and per-tool-call.
user_stories: As a product engineer, I want to show the user partial, human-legible suggestions during generation so the UI feels responsive and useful before final text is ready.
As a platform engineer building a tool integration, I want the runtime to guarantee a single canonical tool-call event (with idempotency tokens) so downstream services see consistent inputs.
As an SDK consumer, I want a small set of client-side primitives (stream iterator, typed event handlers) so I don't wire my own parsing and error handling.
As an SRE, I want per-frame latency and token counts exported so I can measure tradeoffs between progressive outputs and cost.
As a security reviewer, I want the handshake to indicate whether the session allows external tool invocation and which tool scopes are active.
As a mobile app developer, I want resumable sessions so an intermittent network doesn't force user-visible regressions or duplicated side-effects from tool-calls.
requirements: Protocol: define an evented framing model (frame types: progress, patch, action, commit, error, meta) that is transport-agnostic (SSE/WebSocket/HTTP streaming).

Tool calling semantics: every action frame must carry a client-visible action_id and an idempotency token; server must provide an action_ack frame once the action is accepted by the orchestration layer.
Progressive legibility: intermediate frames should include a "legibility_score" heuristic and an optional "stable_prefix" indicating committed text that won't be edited by later patches.
Patch model: support patch operations that are mergeable (operational transform-like simple ops: append, replace-range, delete-range) to avoid full-text re-sends.
SDK ergonomics: SDKs should provide both pull (async iterator) and push (callback/handler) surfaces, plus a small "ActionClient" helper to manage action lifecycles and retries.
Resumability: durable_session_id token returned at start; client can resume with last_seen_frame_seq to replay missed frames; server must ensure replay is idempotent for action frames.
Backpressure: client can advertise window_size and preferred_latency SLO in handshake; server uses this to choose batching/flush heuristics.
Observability: per-frame metrics (tokens_emitted, frame_type, model_variant, cpu_ms, gpu_ms) emitted to the Console and available via trace links in frames of type meta.
Security: explicit tool scope declaration in initial handshake (list of tool ids allowed) and optional confirmable tool-call mode where user must explicitly confirm tool invocation before execution.
Migration: backward compatibility flags so older SDKs receive a simpler 'chunk' stream without frame types and the server falls back to legacy streaming semantics.
sdk_patterns: Simple iterator (recommended for server-driven UI): for await frame of client.stream() { switch(frame.type) { case 'progress': renderPartial(frame); break; case 'patch': applyPatch(frame.ops); break; case 'action': actionClient.queue(frame); break; }}
Event handler (callback): client.on('progress', cb), client.on('patch', cb), client.on('commit', cb')

ActionClient helper: allocate action_id, attach idempotency token, expose action.promise that resolves when action_ack+result arrives or rejects on error. SDK retries should be configurable and respect server 'action_ack' to prevent duplicates.
Mobile-optimized sample: minimal handler that accepts only 'stable_prefix' and 'commit' frames; SDK collapses intermediate patches to reduce allocations.
HTTP fallback: POST /v1/generate with prefer: sync-streaming header returns multipart/mixed stream; if client doesn't accept frames, server emits legacy 'chunk' events maintaining compatibility.
telemetry_and_slo: Emit a 'frame.metrics' meta event every 10 frames or on commit with tokens_emitted and cpu_ms/gpu_ms. Key SLOs: p50 time-to-first-progress (<120ms on hosted tier), p95 to first stable_prefix (<450ms), p99 action_ack latency (<200ms internal). Chargeable units: tokens_emitted per final committed token plus small per-action orchestration charge. Export traces to Console with links included in action_ack/meta frames for quick debugging.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - experiments (2 weeks): server-side feature flag, internal SDK build for web + node, enable telemetry, test across representative apps (chat, code-assist, customer support summarizer).
Phase 1 - partner beta (4 weeks): invite 3 integrators, collect SDK ergonomics feedback, refine action idempotency guarantees and patch ops. Monitor double-invocation and resume corner cases.
Phase 2 - public opt-in (2 months): enable via API param for hosted customers, default to legacy streaming for older clients. Provide migration guide and example apps.
Phase 3 - default (after metrics ok): flip default to progressive frames for new sessions and document cost model changes in pricing pages.
open_questions: Operator model: should action execution be synchronous (server executes and returns result) or fire-and-forget with separate callback? Which is simpler to reason about for idempotency?
Patch semantics: do we need full OT/CRDT or will simple replace/append/delete suffice for our primary use-cases?
Resumes + tool-calls: on resume, do we replay action frames or only replay client-visible frames and require client to re-attach to action state?
Client-side UX: how do we convey that a partial suggestion is "stable" vs likely-to-change without overstating confidence? Standardize legibility_score thresholds?
Pricing model: what is fair for per-action orchestration cost vs token count to avoid surprising customers?
dependencies_and_risks: Serving runtime: need support for attaching small per-request runtime traces and emitting per-frame metrics (INFR-3472).
Console: trace viewer needs to surface per-action traces and link from frames (CONSOLE-121).
Client SDKs: work for web/node/mobile required; must coordinate with devexp team for release timelines.
Compatibility: risk of breaking existing streaming clients; mitigation via handshake flags and a clear migration path.
Security: tool scoping enforcement must be plumbed through auth layer to avoid privilege escalation.
Operational complexity: additional orchestration state for action acks and durable sessions increases surface area for bugs and long-lived connections cost.
